newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil lower house telecom vote expected Wed.
newsitem.headline: Brazil lower house telecom vote expected Wed.

text.p: Congress' lower house was expected to vote Wednesday on a bill regulating Brazil's telecoms sector and outlining the privatization of the federal Telebras system, an official said.
"They're meeting now. It should happen this morning," said a spokesman for Deputy Alberto Goldman, who drafted the bill.

The Chamber of Deputies also were to vote on proposed amendments to the General Telecommunications Law bill, including one striking an article that would give firms the right to set their own rates after three years.

The amendments, which contain the most controversial aspects of the legislation, also include such key points as foreign capital participation in new private telecom operators and guidelines for creating a new sector watchdog.
Goldman read his draft to lawmakers at a special session late Tuesday and analysts said the bill suffered several important changes, most to be voted on in the amendments.
A lower house vote had been expected earlier this month after the measure was approved by a 21-7 vote by a special chamber panel in May.
But lawmakers repeatedly delay the vote to give themselves more time to discuss the bill.
If approved by deputies, the bill would be sent to the Senate for a final nod.
